title: Ozone and moisture gave no clear repeated link to injury burden at injured eastern US forest sites in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether ozone and moisture had a repeated joint link to injury burden at sites with visible leaf injury. We reused a verified public-data panel and split two eastern US regions into 1994-2002 and 2003-2010. The positive-index models used 1,642 site-years. They controlled site and year effects, curved exposures, visit date, temperature and plant sampling. Three of four interaction slopes were negative. All four intervals included zero after correction for four tests. The early Northeast slope was positive under a marginal 95 percent interval, but this did not repeat. Models of injury presence also gave no clear repeated link. Earlier evidence for injury presence therefore does not establish the same pattern for burden among injured sites. Selection on injury can itself create associations. Few clusters, estimated exposure, missed injury and shared source records limit inference. This is a descriptive model audit, not a causal test or evidence that ozone is safe. The package includes code, aggregate results, source hashes and a verified retrieval recipe. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Interaction slopes for injury presence and log injury burden at injured sites. Thin blue lines show four-test intervals. Thick gray lines show marginal 95 percent intervals. The two panels use different outcome units and selected samples.

citations.reason: Verified analysis panel reused. All source records overlap. We test positive injury burden as a separate outcome.
Product decomposition, regional periods and occurrence model provide the comparison. Code was written anew.
